placements.role: Provides outsourced advanced packaging and test for high-performance-compute and AI semiconductors.

role_evidence.claim: Amkor's official release says it provides advanced packaging and test, including turnkey services for TSMC customers using advanced wafer fabrication.

business_summary: Amkor Technology, Inc. is a NASDAQ-listed outsourced semiconductor assembly and test provider: it packages and tests other companies' silicon rather than fabricating it. That makes it a toll-taker on unit volume and on packaging complexity, not on wafer pricing. Its exposure to this chain is the advanced-packaging step, where 2.5D, high-density fan-out and system-in-package capacity has repeatedly been the gate on accelerator output rather than wafer starts.

exposure_summary.narrative: One placement, on advanced-packaging, position 7 of the chain and a CHOKE_POINT link whose heat verdict is EMERGING rather than CROWDED. Amkor is the purest listed way to hold the outsourced side of that step: unlike TSMC, Intel or the memory makers it has no fab and no design business diluting the packaging line. The placement is backed by Amkor's own dated release on its TSMC turnkey partnership.

disclosed_revenue_exposure.basis: Amkor reports by end market (communications, computing, automotive and industrial, consumer), not by packaging technology, so no disclosed percentage of revenue attributable to AI or high-performance-computing advanced packaging exists in a source read this run.

implied_fcf_cagr.basis: Free-cash-flow CAGR the current enterprise value 11976840640 implies over a 5-year explicit period on base FCF 190992000, solved by bisection at a 0.09 discount rate and 0.025 terminal growth. The discount rate and terminal growth are assumed, so this is an assumption-dependent expectation reading, not a reported figure. The base FCF is small relative to enterprise value, which is what drives the high solve.

horizon_spread.basis: Spread between the implied CAGR solved over the shortest and longest explicit periods in quality.reverse_dcf.implied_by_horizon ({'5': 0.3832, '7': 0.2804, '10': 0.2085}). It measures how much of the expectation reading is a horizon convention rather than a statement about price, and inherits the same assumed discount rate and terminal growth.

crowdedness_caveats: data/market/AMKR.json carries no pcs block, so analyst count and institutional ownership were not measured for this issuer this run; crowdedness here rests on the chain link's heat, not on a coverage reading of the stock.

The advanced-packaging link's heat verdict is EMERGING with crowdedness 55 and capture 60 (data/chains/ai-infrastructure.json), the least crowded of the four links this batch touches. That is a statement about the link, not about this ticker.
The 52-week range is 23.80 to 93.55 against a 47.88 close: the stock has roughly halved from its own high. A drawdown is not evidence of being un-crowded.

Three-year revenue CAGR is negative. An issuer whose revenue is below its 2022 level is not obviously the same story as the AI packaging bottleneck, and the gap between those two facts is the thing a dive would have to close.

catalysts.claim: Amkor's own dated release establishes a turnkey advanced-packaging relationship with TSMC, which is the mechanism by which outsourced packaging capacity is attached to leading-edge wafer supply.
Cash conversion is strong: operating cash flow is 2.93x net income for fiscal 2025, so the business funds a heavy capital programme from operations rather than from the balance sheet.

confidence_audit.basis: Counts cover the canonical metric fields only. VERIFIED is a figure read directly off SEC companyfacts as reported. SPECULATIVE is reserved for the reverse-DCF solve, whose discount rate and terminal growth are assumed. NULL is a field looked for and not found, never estimated.
